presets.ultra: Everything, full-size textures, longest view. Hours to build, and only an ultra card runs it.
presets.high: Everything at 512 px. The default, and what the reference city is validated at.
presets.performance: Everything, smaller textures and fewer drawn triangles. For an 8 GB card at high resolution.
presets.medium: 60 % of the trees, 70 % of the props, 3 km view. A mid-range card.
presets.low: Roads, buildings and a third of the foliage. What runs on a laptop.

settings.help: Bundle directory. The app finds the ripper mod's own export folder by itself; this overrides it
settings.label: Bundle folder
settings.blurb: The folder Cities: Skylines II wrote when you ripped your city.

settings.help: Levels directory to write into (default: the BeamNG userfolder levels/)
settings.label: Levels folder
settings.blurb: Where BeamNG keeps its levels. Your finished level is written in here.

settings.help: Level folder name (lowercase, underscores)
settings.label: Folder name
settings.blurb: The name of the folder your level is written into. Letters, digits and dashes.

settings.help: Level title shown in BeamNG
settings.label: Level title
settings.blurb: The name shown in the level list once it is built.

settings.help: BeamNG executable (auto-detected when empty)
settings.label: BeamNG
settings.blurb: Where the game is installed. Filled in for you when it was found on this machine.

settings.help: Build one square patch of the city instead of all of it: X Z half-width, in bundle metres
settings.label: Area
settings.blurb: Build the whole city, or one square patch of it. A smaller piece builds far faster.

settings.help: Buildings
settings.label: Buildings
settings.blurb: Houses, offices, factories and everything else your city has built.

settings.help: Roads, rails and other network meshes
settings.label: Roads and rails
settings.blurb: Road, rail and path surfaces, and the ground opened up at trenches and tunnels.

settings.help: Road markings and painted decals (pre-draped)
settings.label: Road markings
settings.blurb: Lane lines, arrows, crossings and the rest of the paint on the tarmac.

settings.help: Roadside furniture: fences, hedges, cables
settings.label: Roadside furniture
settings.blurb: Fences, hedges and overhead cables that run alongside the roads.

settings.help: Furniture categories to include
settings.label: Kinds to include
settings.blurb: Which sorts of roadside detail get built. Clearing them all leaves none of it.

settings.help: Painted surfaces (parking lots, paths)
settings.label: Painted surfaces
settings.blurb: Car parks, plazas, footpaths and the other flat coloured ground.

settings.help: Building foundation skirts
settings.label: Building foundations
settings.blurb: The strip of wall that fills the gap where a plot meets sloping ground.

settings.help: Street and building lights (dynamic lights are expensive)
settings.label: Street and building lights
settings.blurb: Lamps, floodlights and lit signs glow after dark. Heavy on your graphics card.

settings.help: Water planes/blocks
settings.label: Water
settings.blurb: Rivers, lakes and the sea.

settings.help: Billboard grass over the ground paint. BeamNG dressing, not CS2 fidelity - CS2 has no grass system
settings.label: Grass
settings.blurb: Blades of grass over the ground. Dressing for the eye; your city has none.

settings.help: Percent of trees kept (deterministic subset)
settings.label: Trees
settings.blurb: How much of the planting to keep. At zero none of it is placed at all.

settings.help: Percent of props kept
settings.label: Props and fences
settings.blurb: How many of the small street objects to keep. At zero none are placed.

settings.help: The distance in metres past which nothing is drawn at all
settings.label: How far you can see
settings.blurb: The distance in metres past which nothing is drawn. The biggest lever on speed.

settings.help: Time of day in hours 0-24 for the level's sun (-1 = the in-game clock at rip time)
settings.label: Time of day
settings.blurb: What hour the sun sits at, either your city's own or one you pick.

settings.help: Collision detail
settings.label: Detail
settings.blurb: Exact shapes, simple boxes, or nothing solid at all. Boxes are far lighter.

settings.help: Buildings collide
settings.label: Buildings
settings.blurb: Cars stop at the walls instead of driving through them.

settings.help: Props collide
settings.label: Props
settings.blurb: Benches, bins and signs are solid.

settings.help: Trees collide (trunk)
settings.label: Trees
settings.blurb: Trunks stop a car. The leaves never do.

settings.help: Fences and lane furniture collide
settings.label: Fences and roadside detail
settings.blurb: Barriers, hedges and cable poles stop a car.

settings.help: Foundation skirts collide
settings.label: Foundations
settings.blurb: The strip under a plot is solid, so you cannot drive into the gap.

settings.help: Markings and painted surfaces collide (not recommended)
settings.label: Markings and painted ground
settings.blurb: Paint is solid too. Usually a mistake: it sits just above the road surface.

settings.help: Props narrower than this (metres) do not collide
settings.label: Ignore objects narrower than
settings.blurb: Anything thinner than this across is driven straight through.

settings.help: Street lights and every other light-bearing prop collide. Off: a 10 m pole stops a car dead
settings.label: Lampposts
settings.blurb: A pole stops a car dead. Off by default because it is the thing you hit most.

settings.help: Colour texture edge cap in pixels (0 = full size). Also caps the emissive and opacity maps
settings.label: Texture detail
settings.blurb: The largest a colour picture may be, in pixels. The main cost on your card.

settings.help: How large a surface-bumpiness picture may be, in pixels (0 = as large as it came)
settings.label: Surface bumpiness detail
settings.blurb: How finely bricks, planks and grooves are described. Lower is flatter and lighter.

settings.help: Edge cap for data maps in pixels: roughness, metallic and the CS2 colour mask
settings.label: Shine and roughness detail
settings.blurb: How finely wet, matt and metal surfaces are described. Rarely needs to be large.

settings.help: Compress the textures during the build, so the game never has to on the first load
settings.label: Prepare textures during the build
settings.blurb: Do the compression now instead of the first time you play. Leave this on.

settings.help: Which sorts of object take their colour from your city; the rest draw an untinted one
settings.label: What gets recoloured
settings.blurb: Which sorts of object take their colour from the city. The rest draw an untinted one.

settings.help: How many shades each kind of plant comes in. Every shade is another copy to draw
settings.label: Shades per kind of plant
settings.blurb: How many shades each kind of plant comes in. More is prettier and heavier.

settings.help: How many shades each kind of small object comes in. One is its average colour
settings.label: Shades per kind of prop
settings.blurb: How many shades each kind of small object comes in.

settings.help: Colour cap for a paint variant's tinted albedo, separately from the main colour cap
settings.label: Recoloured texture detail
settings.blurb: How large the recoloured copies may be, in pixels.

settings.help: Lighten or darken the ground. One leaves it as your city has it
settings.label: Ground brightness
settings.blurb: Lighten or darken the grass, sand and dirt. One leaves them as your city has them.

settings.help: Terrain grid: 2 = 8192 at 1.75 m (the game's own near-camera detail); 1 = 4096 at 3.5 m, lighter
settings.label: Ground detail
settings.blurb: How finely the ground is shaped. Higher is sharper underfoot and costs memory.

settings.help: The invisible road network the AI, the minimap and route-finding use. Off = no minimap and no routes
settings.label: Minimap and routing
settings.blurb: Lets the minimap, route markers and traffic use the roads. Off leaves the map blank.

settings.help: Let routes run across the apron and the taxiways too, slowly
settings.label: Include airport taxiways
settings.blurb: Let routes run across the apron and the taxiways, slowly.

settings.help: Fast-travel points on the big map, derived from the densest road cells
settings.label: Fast-travel points
settings.blurb: Places you can jump straight to from the big map.

settings.help: The file holding the fast-travel points you named, instead of the ones picked for you
settings.label: Your own fast-travel points
settings.blurb: Places you name and put on the map yourself, instead of the ones picked for you.

settings.help: How many busy places to pick out for you when you have named fewer of your own
settings.label: How many to suggest
settings.blurb: How many busy spots to pick out for you when you have named none of your own.

settings.help: Generate LOD chains for every shape
settings.label: Generate LOD chains
settings.blurb: Build reduced-triangle LOD levels for every shape. Off ships LOD 0 at every distance.

settings.help: Give the merged world tiles (roads, markings, areas, skirts, furniture) a real LOD chain
settings.label: LOD chains for world tiles
settings.blurb: Give the merged road, marking, area, skirt and furniture tiles an LOD chain of their own.

settings.help: Engine-generated billboard imposters (bb_autobillboard)
settings.label: Billboard imposters
settings.blurb: Let BeamNG render a distant shape to a billboard atlas. Cheap to draw, and visibly flat.

settings.help: Only give an imposter to a shape still drawn beyond this distance; 0 = 3/4 of the view distance
settings.label: Imposter minimum cull distance
settings.blurb: A shape culled nearer than this gets no billboard atlas. 0 derives it from the far cull.

settings.help: How many times closer than CS2 an object is culled. 1 = exactly what the game draws
settings.label: Cull distance divisor
settings.blurb: Divide every shape's CS2 cull distance by this. 1 reproduces what the game itself draws.

settings.help: The same multiplier as lod_detail_scale but for PROPS only; 0 = use the global one
settings.label: Cull distance divisor, props
settings.blurb: The cull divisor applied to props alone. 0 makes props share the global divisor.

settings.help: How many pixels of surface error a generated LOD may show when it takes over. Smaller = truer, heavier
settings.label: LOD switch error budget
settings.blurb: Screen-space error in pixels a generated LOD may show as it takes over. Lower is truer.

settings.help: Drop LOD0 where LOD1 is within this many metres of it
settings.label: LOD 0 promotion threshold
settings.blurb: Drop LOD 0 where LOD 1's p95 surface deviation is within this many metres. 0 keeps every one.

settings.help: ...but never where that leaves the shape shipping fewer triangles than this. 0 = no floor
settings.label: LOD 0 promotion floor
settings.blurb: Never promote where that would leave the shape shipping fewer triangles than this.

settings.help: Merge a forest type holding fewer items than this into its prefab's plain type. 0 keeps every type
settings.label: Forest type merge threshold
settings.blurb: A forest type holding fewer items than this is merged into its prefab's untinted type.

settings.help: Triangle budget for baked lane furniture, 0 = no budget. What goes first is what CS2 culls first
settings.label: Baked lane furniture budget
settings.blurb: Triangle ceiling for the sheared fence and cable tiles, spent in CS2's own cull order.

settings.help: How far a paint variant may drift, in 8-bit channels, before it gets a texture of its own
settings.label: colorSet factor tolerance
settings.blurb: How far a colorSet variant may drift, in 8-bit channels, before it gets its own texture.

settings.help: Declared deviation: drop a tree standing this close to a lane centre so the city can be driven. 0 = off
settings.label: Lane clearance for trees
settings.blurb: Declared deviation: drop a tree whose trunk is within this of a drivable lane centre.

settings.help: Forest items cast shadows
settings.label: Forest shadow casting
settings.blurb: Forest items cast shadows. One of the heaviest per-frame costs a dense canopy carries.

settings.help: Synthesise wind vertex colours for trees
settings.label: Synthesised wind vertex colours
settings.blurb: Write wind weights into tree vertex colours so BeamNG animates them. CS2 records no wind.

settings.help: World tile size for roads/markings/areas (metres)
settings.label: World tile size
settings.blurb: Edge length of the merged road, marking, area and skirt tiles.

settings.help: Which clip cells become terrain holes
settings.label: Terrain hole rule
settings.blurb: Which clip-volume cells are punched out of the heightfield as terrain holes.

settings.help: Ground-boundary interlock, x the derived amount. 1 = faithful; 2-3 hides the blocky material edges
settings.label: Ground blend interlock
settings.blurb: Multiplier on BeamNG's derived layer-blend sharpness. 1 is faithful, higher is neater.

settings.help: Maximum dynamic lights (needs Advanced Lighting in BeamNG)
settings.label: Dynamic light ceiling
settings.blurb: Ceiling on punctual lights placed, ranked by BeamNG's own importance metric.

settings.help: Clamp a navgraph node's road width, in metres (0 = the width CS2's own lane offsets give)
settings.label: Navgraph node radius clamp
settings.blurb: Clamp a navgraph node's road width. 0 uses the width CS2's own lane offsets give.

settings.help: Dedicated VRAM of the card the level is for, in MiB (0 = read it from your own beamng.log)
settings.label: Dedicated VRAM
settings.blurb: How much memory the card this level is built for has. 0 reads it from your own BeamNG log.

settings.help: Render width the level is for (0 = read it from beamng.log)
settings.label: Render width
settings.blurb: Horizontal render resolution this level is built for. 0 reads it from your own BeamNG log.

settings.help: Render height the level is FOR (0 = read it from beamng.log, fall back to 1080)
settings.label: Render height
settings.blurb: Vertical render resolution this level is built for. 0 reads it from your own BeamNG log.

settings.help: Worker processes for parallel stages (0 = CPU count - 1)
settings.label: Worker processes
settings.blurb: Parallel worker processes for the multiprocess stages. 0 leaves one core free.

settings.help: Compile the shapes with BeamNG's own compiler after the build, so the first load is fast
settings.label: Cook shapes after the build
settings.blurb: Run BeamNG's headless mesh compiler over the level so the first load does not have to.

settings.help: Rebuild every stage from scratch, ignoring what the last build recorded
settings.label: Force a full rebuild
settings.blurb: Ignore the recorded stage state and run every stage from scratch.

settings.help: Keep a partially built level after cancel
settings.label: Keep a cancelled level
settings.blurb: Leave a partially built level on disk after a cancel instead of removing it.

settings.help: Delete cooked shapes in BeamNG's temp/ that this level no longer has
settings.label: Sweep BeamNG's temp folder
settings.blurb: Delete cooked shapes in BeamNG's temp folder that this level no longer references.

settings.help: Keep .dae sources beside the cooked .cdae (off saves ~5 GB, forces a full recook next build)
settings.label: Keep the COLLADA sources
settings.blurb: The .dae sources stay beside the cooked .cdae. Off saves disk and forces a full recook.

settings.help: Where the UI opens: a native window, a named browser, or the system default
settings.label: UI host
settings.blurb: Where this window opens: a native window, a named browser, or the system default.

settings.help: Trees (forest)
settings.label: Trees on or off
settings.blurb: Whether any planting is placed at all.

settings.help: Props, fences, points of interest
settings.label: Props on or off
settings.blurb: Whether any small street objects are placed at all.

settings.help: Cut the ground open at trenches and tunnel portals and drop the exact cut mesh into the hole
settings.label: Cut the ground at tunnels
settings.blurb: Open the ground at trenches and tunnel mouths and drop the cut mesh into the hole.

settings.help: Quality preset last applied
settings.label: Quality preset
settings.blurb: The named quality level the settings were last set from.

settings.help: The settings section the UI opens on (remembered between sessions)
settings.label: Last settings section
settings.blurb: Which part of the settings you had open. Remembered between sessions.
